<thought>Based on the observed isotopic pattern—a dominant peak with a modest M+1 (~8 % of base) and a rapidly diminishing M+2 (~0.5 % of base)—the only element whose natural isotopic distribution matches this behavior is carbon (13C contributes to M+1, and the low M+2 arises from the probability of two 13C atoms). No characteristic chlorine, bromine, or sulfur patterns are present, and other elements have isotopic contributions too small to be distinguished. Therefore, carbon can be definitively identified.</thought>
<final_answer>['C']</final_answer>
